html:
The Caxcan are an Indigenous people of western Mexico, in what is now southern Zacatecas and northern Jalisco. They spoke a language close to Nahuatl, of the Uto-Aztecan family, and farmed maize in the canyons north of Guadalajara.

They are best known for leading the Mixtón War of 1540 to 1542, the largest revolt against early Spanish rule in western Mexico. Angered by forced labour and slave raids under Nuño de Guzmán, they and their neighbours rose under the leader Tenamaxtli and held the fortified hill of Mixtón. The rising was so dangerous that the viceroy Antonio de Mendoza himself led a large army of Spaniards and Indigenous allies to crush it, and the conquistador Pedro de Alvarado was killed in the fighting. Their neighbours included the Zacatecos and the Tecuexe. Their language died out in the late 1800s.
